summary: Agent implemented the checkbox directly in index.html on the first turn, with no brainstorming skill invocation and no clarifying questions.
reasoning: The single user message led directly to an Edit inserting a native checkbox; the session log confirms zero Skill tool calls, so brainstorming was not over-triggered. Both acceptance criteria pass. Noted separately that the token-usage artifact the story references was not present on disk.

observations.description: No coding-agent-token-usage.json file was produced in the run results directory (`ls` shows only coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home, phase.json), so the headline token-cost measurement this scenario exists to collect is not available at the location the story names.

Claude Code startup required four separate confirmation prompts (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions) before any input was possible, despite the launcher being described as pre-seeded with dialog-bypass state.
Transient spinner label rendered as "Bunning…" (looks like a garbled/randomized gerund) while the agent was thinking.
Agent added an unrequested CSS strike-through rule for checked items despite "nothing fancy"; minor scope addition, though it also offered persistence as a follow-up rather than doing it.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Single static HTML file, no framework or build — this is a one-file edit, so I'll make it directly." then Update(index.html) adding `<input type="checkbox">`. Session log tool_use sequence was only Bash (git status/ls), Read(index.html), Edit(index.html). `grep -n checkbox coding-agent-workdir/index.html` → `16:        <input type="checkbox">`

`grep -c '"name":"Skill"' home/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl` → 0. The only 'brainstorming' matches in the log are system-prompt/skill-list text (e.g. skill names list "hyperpowers:brainstorming"), not tool invocations.
